property_summary: For every call to version(), the reference contract always returns the string "1.0.0"; the mutant returns a different string for some inputs (breaking this invariant).

For all inputs, calling c.version() returns the exact string "1.0.0" on the reference contract; the mutant that changes the returned string to "1.0.1" violates this rule for some inputs (the call without arguments), so the fuzz test asserts the returned string equals "1.0.0" and will fail against the mutant.

For every call, the reference contract's version() returns the non-empty string "1.0.0" (i.e., a non-empty string), whereas the mutant can return an empty string, so the property is that version()'s returned length is > 0 for all inputs and the bug produces length == 0 for some input.

For every call to version() the reference contract returns the string "1.0.0"; the mutant changes the returned string so some calls will return a different string (e.g. "0.0.0"), violating this invariant.

For all calls, the reference contract's version() returns the exact string "1.0.0"; the mutant returns a different string for some input (e.g., when called normally), so comparing the returned string equality to "1.0.0" distinguishes them.
Only the depositorAccount can successfully call setL1BlockValues (calls from other accounts revert).
Calls to setL1BlockValues revert for every caller address that is not equal to c.depositorAccount().

For any caller address X, calling setL1BlockValues must only succeed when msg.sender equals the depositorAccount stored in the contract; the mutant that checks msg.sender == address(this) will reject valid depositor callers (or allow none) and thus violate this invariant for some fuzzed depositor addresses.

For any caller address, calling setL1BlockValues on the reference contract always reverts unless the caller is the mutable depositorAccount (so non-equal to the hardcoded DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT when depositorAccount differs); the mutant which checks the constant DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT instead allows the hardcoded address to succeed and thus violates the invariant that calls from arbitrary addresses (including the hardcoded one when depositorAccount is different) cannot set L1 values — the fuzzer can pick depositorAccount and caller to expose the difference.
